sources.title: Philip J. Deloria, “What Is the Middle Ground, Anyway?” (2006).
sources.citation: Philip J. Deloria, “What Is the Middle Ground, Anyway?,” William and Mary Quarterly, third series, 63, no. 1 (January 2006): 15–22.

verification.note: Complete original eight-page article and notes read in a single-article teaching share linked by the University of British Columbia HIST594 2018 reading schedule; printed 22 visually collated. Admiring reception at 15–19 and 22 is retained alongside place/process, metaphor and balanced-power objections at 19–22. No fresh full reading of White’s 1991 book or all cited works. Canonical link identifies the journal original.

iha_fontella_white_2022.note: Fresh original journal PDF retrieved from SciELO, byte-identical to retained witness; title/translation statement at 1 and complete interview answers 9–17 read, with selected editorial discussion 4–7. Written English exchange received 30 April 2021, freely translated into Portuguese by Fontella, published 2022. Giddens 13/16, Dening 13, Sahlins 13, Clifford/Wolf and qualified Lévi-Strauss 14, paired Cronon/Worster positions 10–11 distinguished. Interviewer prompts, editorial historical claims, bibliographic notes and White’s answers remain separate. Full editorial introduction and all notes not read; no fresh originals of cited books.

pe131_richard_white_middle_ground_prefac.note: Fresh complete 2011 twentieth-anniversary preface xi–xxiv and all 35 notes read in Cambridge’s publisher frontmatter PDF; imprint explicitly dates this edition 2011, unlike the landing page’s 2010 field and later online posting. Scott xiv/notes6–9; Deloria xii/note1; Lévi-Strauss xiii and xvii–xix; Dening xx–xxi; Havard xvi–xix and Merrell xix–xxiv checked. The 1991 book body and cited originals remain unread. Apparent note28 mismatch at xx is not silently corrected or used as verified Merrell bibliographic evidence.

hr28_wiebe_white2017.note: Fresh original university department interview repost read in full, by Alex Shashkevich, dated 25 October 2017; linked original News Service item is a separate manifestation. White’s joint Hofstadter/Wiebe criticism and specific Hofstadter individualism objection occur in consecutive interpretation/misconception answers. His personal project account credits David Kennedy’s invitation but does not prove a broader intellectual debt; complete White, Wiebe and Hofstadter books remain unread.
